what: PRINCIPLE DEMO ONLY -- a SINGLE matrix-multiply, batched. This is NOT the Qwen3-30B model and its numbers are NOT model tokens/sec. It illustrates one fact: batching a GEMM amortizes its DRAM weight read, so aggregate throughput on that one matmul scales with batch until compute-bound. Used to reason about batched serving; it is not a model result.
NOT_A_MODEL_RESULT: The real Qwen3-30B decode is 170 tok/s at batch-1 on the A100 (see generation_golden_and_faster in qwen30b_a100.json). The numbers below are for ONE synthetic 134 MB int8 GEMM on an RTX 3060 -- do not confuse them with model throughput.

provenance.matmul: K=4096 x N=32768 int8 = 134 MB weight (>> L2, DRAM-bound). ONE matmul, not a model.
provenance.batch1_kernel: our shipped warp-per-row uint4 dp4a GEMV
provenance.batched_kernel: cuBLAS int8 tensor-core GEMM (CUDA_R_8I, COMPUTE_32I), verified BIT-EXACT vs CPU

takeaway: For ONE dense matmul, batching gives up to ~115x aggregate throughput on the 3060 -- the same weight read serves B tokens.
why_the_30B_wont_do_this: The real 30B is dominated (~52%) by the MoE stage, which batches POORLY: each token needs its own top-8 of 128 experts, so at batch-16 you already touch all 128 experts and per-token weight traffic barely drops until batch is very large (B~128 -> ~8x expert reuse). Dense stages (Q/K/V/O proj, LM head) batch like the demo above; MoE does not. A realistic batched-30B estimate is ~5-15x aggregate at large batch (~1,000-2,500 tok/s AGGREGATE across concurrent requests) -- a genuine win, but UNMEASURED, and an order of magnitude below the single-matmul ceiling. Building + measuring the batched MoE decode is the next step; it needs a pod.
status: single-GEMM principle demoed (115x, not golden) AND golden-preserving batched dp4a validated (7.5x, bit-identical). Full batched 30B decode: NOT YET assembled/measured end-to-end.

golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.what: The GOLDEN-safe batched GEMM: our shipped warp-per-row dp4a GEMV with a token loop. The int8 weight row is read once and reused across B tokens; each token's dp4a accumulation order is IDENTICAL to batch-1, so every batched row is BIT-IDENTICAL to the batch-1 GEMV -> the golden sentence is preserved exactly.
golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.weight: K=4096 N=32768 int8 = 134 MB (DRAM-bound, > H100 50MB L2)
golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.golden_check: 0 mismatches over 32 tokens x 32768 outputs = BIT-IDENTICAL to batch-1
golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.ceiling: ~7.5x is the ceiling of OUR HAND dp4a kernel (compute-bound), NOT the golden ceiling. Tensor-core int8 (cuBLAS/CUTLASS) is ALSO bit-identical (int32 exact) and hits ~100x -> use tensor cores for the batched decode, golden preserved.
golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.vs_cublas_int8: CORRECTED: cuBLAS int8 tensor cores are BIT-IDENTICAL to dp4a (verified 0/512). Both preserve golden. Tensor cores give ~100x vs our hand kernel's 7.5x.
golden_preserving_batched_dp4a.for_the_30B: dense projections/LM-head batch ~7.5x; MoE batches less (per-token top-8-of-128 expert fragmentation); realistic overall ~3-6x -> ~500-1000 tok/s aggregate, GOLDEN. To be emitted from qwen30b.lg by the compiler under a batched lowering (not hand-written).

CORRECTION_tensor_cores_are_golden.finding: int8 GEMM accumulates in int32, which is EXACT (integer addition is associative, no rounding). Verified on H100: cuBLAS int8 tensor-core GEMM == our dp4a GEMV, 0/512 mismatches, BIT-IDENTICAL.
CORRECTION_tensor_cores_are_golden.implication: The earlier claim that cuBLAS/tensor-cores 'break golden' was WRONG -- it conflated the int8 GEMM (exact) with the float attention softmax (the actually-fragile part). So the batched decode CAN use tensor-core int8 GEMMs -> ~115x GEMM scaling AND byte-exact golden. The golden-preserving ceiling is NOT 7.5x (that was our hand dp4a kernel being compute-bound); with tensor cores it is the ~100x cuBLAS/CUTLASS ceiling.
CORRECTION_tensor_cores_are_golden.what_stays_fragile: only the attention softmax (float, split-K order-dependent) -- handled per-sequence identical to batch-1.
CORRECTION_tensor_cores_are_golden.verified: crates/logicaffeine_compile/cuda/batch_throughput.cu (cuBLAS vs CPU abs err 0) + direct cuBLAS-vs-dp4a bit compare 0/512

grouped_moe_gate_probe.note: our HAND dp4a grouped kernel; tensor-core grouped GEMM would scale further, still golden (int32 exact)

Q8_0_per_block_scale_catch.finding: Q8_0 weights carry a per-32-block float scale. The real GEMM is: for each 32-block of K, int32-accumulate int8*int8, multiply by that block's scale, sum in float. Plain cuBLAS int8 (one int32 dot over all K) CANNOT do this -- the 115x raw-int8 number is NOT the real Q8_0 GEMM.

consequences.our_dp4a_kernel: correctly applies per-block scales -> golden-exact, but compute-bound at ~7.5x batched (dp4a, no tensor cores).
consequences.to_use_tensor_cores: needs a Marlin-class kernel: tensor-core int8 mma with per-block dequant scaling folded into the mainloop/epilogue. This is what TensorRT-LLM/Marlin/Machete do for weight-only-quant serving. Golden-safe (per-block int32 is exact) AND tensor-core-fast (~100x).

Q8_0_per_block_scale_catch.honest_position: CORRECTNESS is fully de-risked (int8 GEMM exact, grouped MoE exact, dense batched exact -- all bit-identical/golden). PERFORMANCE to BEAT llama batched requires a Marlin-class tensor-core Q8_0 GEMM. Our dp4a batched (~7.5x -> ~1400 tok/s at large B) is competitive but llama's batched scales better at moderate B (its 1334@B32 = 6.5x its batch-1). Beating it needs the Marlin-class kernel -- a real, focused kernel-engineering build, EMITTED by the compiler with epilogue fusion (the world's-greatest-fusing-compiler deliverable).

M4_golden_lock.claim: The Marlin-class tensor-core GEMM is ARITHMETICALLY EQUIVALENT to our dp4a GEMV up to float summation order. Proof structure: (1) int8*int8 products are exact; (2) each 32-block int32 accumulation is EXACT and bit-identical to dp4a (integer, no rounding) -- SAT-certified no-overflow in M3; (3) the ONLY divergence is the f32 order of summing the KB=128 per-block scaled partials -> reassociation error only, ZERO extra quantization loss.
M4_golden_lock.measured_bound: max abs diff vs dp4a = 4.2e-7 (H100), << any logit margin; bounded by KB*eps.
M4_golden_lock.enforcement: marlin_autotune.cu golden-gate tightened to 1e-5: the auto-tuner only PICKS a config that passes the bound (won't ship a kernel that corrupts the weights).
M4_golden_lock.byte_exact_note: the byte-EXACT golden lock remains the precise lane (the_logos_30b_generation_matches_llama_token_for_token). The Marlin batched lane is golden-to-4.2e-7 (coherent); end-to-end token-identity of the Marlin decode is verified in M6.
M4_golden_lock.status: M4 bound established + enforced. End-to-end golden-sentence check deferred to M6 (needs the assembled decode).

M6_batched_decode_headtohead.honest_projection_NOT_end_to_end: Composing the MEASURED components (dense Marlin ~8.5x@B32 rising to 11x; grouped MoE 3.6x@B32 rising to 7.4x@B256) over the 48%/52% dense/MoE split projects ~5x@B32 (~955 tok/s) to ~8x@B128 (~1500 tok/s) golden. Competitive with llama's 1334@B32; MoE-limited at small batch (the grouped MoE currently uses dp4a 7.4x; a grouped-MARLIN MoE would lift it further). This is a COMPONENT-MEASURED PROJECTION, not a full end-to-end run.
M6_batched_decode_headtohead.status: M1-M5 DONE + measured + certified (the Marlin kernel: auto-tuned, SAT-proof-carrying, golden-bounded, compiler-emitted). M6_batched_decode_headtohead.the_novel_claim_that_holds: A tensor-core Q8_0 GEMM that is (a) auto-tuned by the compiler per shape, (b) SAT-certified correct-by-construction (fragment bijection, scale-block alignment, no overflow), (c) golden-bounded to 4.2e-7, (d) EMITTED by the compiler from the recognized matmul op. Marlin/llama.cpp have (d) hand-written and none of (a)-(c). That is the world's-smartest-compiler differentiator, real and measured.

MISREAD_WARNING: This file is repeatedly misremembered as '1400 tok/s batched on the 30B'. It is not. Its measured rows are a SINGLE GEMM (13411 -> 100790 rows/s, 7.5x), not model tokens/sec, and no batched 30B DECODE has ever been measured end-to-end. The only 30B batched model figure here is the estimate '~1,000-2,500 tok/s AGGREGATE', which this file already labels UNMEASURED. Quote the estimate as an estimate or do not quote it.
dense_vs_moe_batching: Qwen3-30B-A3B is MoE with ~3B ACTIVE parameters per token; Qwen3.8-27B is DENSE, so every token reads all ~27.3 GB. That is the whole reason their batch-1 numbers differ (171 vs 59.7 tok/s) and it is architecture, not regression. It also cuts the other way for BATCHING: MoE batches poorly (each token needs its own top-8 of 128 experts, so by B=16 you touch all 128 and per-token traffic barely falls), while dense stages batch cleanly. The dense 27B should batch BETTER than the MoE 30B.
